discovery: Discovery of exoplanet transits and their development into a precision method for measuring planetary sizes, demographics and atmospheres

nominees.name: David Charbonneau
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University / Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

motivation: In 1999 Charbonneau and Henry independently observed the first transit of an exoplanet, HD 209458b. This confirmed beyond doubt that the radial-velocity signals were real planets and gave the first direct measurement of a planet's radius and, with Doppler masses, its density. Charbonneau then pioneered transmission and secondary-eclipse spectroscopy, giving the first detection of an exoplanet atmosphere (2002) and of thermal emission (2005). Borucki championed space-based transit photometry for decades against widespread scepticism and led the Kepler mission, whose photometric precision revealed thousands of planets and showed that small, rocky worlds in temperate orbits are common in our Galaxy. Together these contributions made precision photometry the main tool of exoplanet science, created the field of atmospheric characterisation, now central to JWST, and turned the question of Earth-like planets and life elsewhere into a quantitative physical problem.
